concepts.label: managed-object
concepts.gloss: A managed object is an identifiable physical or logical network resource whose operational state is monitored and against which events and alarms are raised.
concepts.example: R7 is a managed router, while bgp-R7-AS64500 is the logical BGP session on R7 toward autonomous system 64500.

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: An event is a point-in-time notification, such as a syslog message or SNMP trap, reporting an occurrence observed on a managed object without necessarily representing an enduring fault condition.
concepts.example: trap-bgp-R7-t0 is an SNMP trap emitted at time t0 to report an occurrence on the bgp-R7-AS64500 session.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: An alarm is a managed indication of an active or tracked fault condition on a resource, annotated with a perceived severity and a standardized probable-cause code and remaining in scope until cleared.
concepts.example: alarm-bgp-R7-down represents the tracked failure of bgp-R7-AS64500 and may carry severity critical and probable cause bgpConnectionLost.

concepts.label: severity
concepts.gloss: Severity is the perceived operational impact or urgency level assigned to an alarm, using ranked values such as critical, major, minor, or warning.
concepts.example: alarm-bgp-R7-down carries severity critical when the lost BGP session causes an immediate, service-affecting routing failure.

concepts.label: probable-cause
concepts.gloss: A probable cause is the standardized diagnostic code carried by an alarm to classify the condition believed to have produced the fault, rather than identifying a definitively proven root cause.
concepts.example: alarm-bgp-R7-down carries holdTimerExpired when R7 declares the BGP session down because no keepalive or update arrived before the hold timer elapsed.

concepts.label: clear
concepts.gloss: A clear is the lifecycle notification or action that resolves a specific outstanding alarm and marks its fault condition as no longer active.
concepts.example: clear-alarm-bgp-R7-down clears alarm-bgp-R7-down after the BGP session to AS64500 is re-established.
